result: The PAVE study aims to recruit up to 100,000 women aged 30-49 years (or 25-49 if living with HIV) across nine countries, anticipating 1000-2000 precancers, with preliminary interim analysis expected by early 2024 and field recruitment completed by end of 2024.
evaluation: One reviewer explicitly noted 'I could not even find how many women were going to be enrolled, the timelines of the study' indicating the protocol lacks clarity on these fundamental design elements. While the manuscript states these details, the reviewer's inability to locate them suggests inadequate presentation of this critical information.

result: The primary objective is to compare sensitivity at a given specificity level of the PAVE approach versus standard of care for triaging HPV-positive women, hypothesizing PAVE will detect more precancer than SOC triage at the same specificity level.
evaluation: One reviewer criticized that 'the statistical methods ("comparing" is not statistics) or the power calculations' were not provided. While the study objective is stated, the lack of detailed statistical methodology and power calculations undermines confidence in the analytical approach.

result: The PAVE strategy combines self-sampled HPV screening using ScreenFire assay with risk-based triage using extended genotyping and AI-assisted automated visual evaluation (AVE) via the Iris device, creating 12 risk strata for management decisions.
evaluation: Multiple reviewers affirmed this as a strength, with one noting it is 'probably the best available combination today' and another stating 'The proposed strategy combined three key innovations to improve an important step in the cervical cancer care continuum.' The editor confirmed it will 'generate convincing evidence regarding the efficacy.'

result: ScreenFire demonstrated >90% concordance with reference HPV DNA assays and 94.2% sensitivity for CIN3+ in validation testing of 2078 stored specimens, similar to Linear Array (93.1%) and TypeSeq (95.9%).
evaluation: One reviewer explicitly noted 'The triage proposed for this study builds on the authors' previously published work in designing the ScreenFire test' as a strength. No reviewers questioned the validation data or performance characteristics of the assay.

result: The protocol specifies collecting biopsies from up to four acetowhite areas, or endocervical sampling if no acetowhite areas are seen, with sites using VIA employing Softbiopsy/SoftECC brush biopsy and colposcopy sites using punch biopsies.
evaluation: One reviewer identified a critical weakness: 'Potential ascertainment bias due to the lack of specified biopsy (such as small four quadrant biopsies or small biopsies across the transformation zone) when aceto-white areas are not identified.' The reviewer noted this 'may not be as sensitive unless clinicians are experienced in endocervical curette procedures' and could 'lead to an over-estimate of sensitivity of the triage approach.'

result: Modeling projections comparing screening versus vaccination showed that a one-time screening campaign would cost ~US$2.5 billion to avert ~570,000 deaths while vaccination would cost ~US$2.0 billion to avert ~640,000 deaths, with screening advancing cancer control by 20 years compared to vaccination's 40-year timeline.
evaluation: One reviewer strongly criticized this analysis: 'Figure 1 comparing screening and vaccination is somewhat misleading. They screen 20 birth cohorts but vaccinate only 5 birth cohorts. Furthermore, the theoretical gains of screening has not really been attained in any country in practise.' The reviewer concluded 'It just seems unnecessary to attack vaccination as a motivation on why screening needs to be modernised.'

result: The effectiveness phase will examine program feasibility, acceptability, and cost-effectiveness using microsimulation modeling to evaluate costs per precancer detected and health/economic implications of different management approaches across risk strata.
evaluation: One reviewer noted 'The inclusion of implementation evaluation in this type of studies is an important milestone in the field of cervical cancer prevention' and emphasized 'results of phase 2 are key to ensure the future implementation of the strategy.' The editor confirmed the trial will generate evidence on 'effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, feasibility and acceptability.'

result: A pilot phase will retrain the AI algorithm for the Iris device, with researchers expecting successful retraining based on similarities to previously tested digital cameras.
evaluation: One reviewer explicitly noted as a strength 'The move from mobile telephone devices to a dedicated device to acquire and evaluate images, overcomes challenges previously encountered whereby updates of mobile phone models required retraining of the AVE algorithm.' No concerns were raised about the retraining approach.

result: A Communication and Retention Workgroup is conducting a mixed-methods pilot study at four sites to explore stakeholders' knowledge, perceptions, and attitudes regarding cervical cancer prevention and screening to inform future dissemination strategies.
evaluation: While not explicitly discussed by reviewers, this component aligns with the broader implementation evaluation that reviewers praised. One reviewer noted the study will 'allow to evaluate efficacy and effectiveness in real-word context' which implicitly supports the communication research component.

result: Data rights and residual biospecimens remain with study site partners, with de-identified data transferred securely through EHAS to NCI contractors, and data can be withdrawn at any time by site partners.
evaluation: No reviewers raised concerns about the data management or ownership structure. The collaborative framework was implicitly supported by reviewers who noted the study's integration into existing screening activities in participating countries.

result: The study has two phases: efficacy (2023-2024) where clinicians are not provided HPV genotyping or AI outputs, followed by effectiveness phase beginning when efficacy is complete if PAVE outperforms standard of care.
evaluation: One reviewer noted as a strength 'The separation of the study into two phases, an efficacy phase in which screen positive people will be triaged and treated according to local standard of care and the performance of AVE will be evaluated against biopsy outcomes will be followed by the second phase.' The phased approach was not questioned.
